title: Go: Advanced Testing
description: Go beyond basic testing with test fixtures, golden files, fuzz testing, and TestMain orchestration.

steps.title: Test fixtures with setup and teardown
steps.description: Write a test that uses a fixture (temporary directory created with `os.MkdirTemp`). Use `t.Cleanup` to remove it. Print fixture creation with `fmt.Printf("Fixture: %s\n", dir)` inside the test function declaration scope.
hints: os.MkdirTemp creates a random temp directory
Cleanup functions run in LIFO order

verification.successMessage: Test fixture with setup and teardown works!

steps.title: Golden file testing
steps.description: Write a test that serializes a struct to JSON, then compares it to a "golden file" in `testdata/`. Use `flag.Update` to update golden files with `-update` flag. Print comparison result using `fmt.Printf("Golden: %s\n", goldenFile)`.
hints: Store expected output in testdata/*.golden files

verification.failureMessage: Print the golden file path and comparison result.

steps.title: Fuzz testing (Fuzz function)
steps.description: Create a `FuzzHexEncoder(f *testing.F)` function that seeds with `f.Add("hello")` and `f.Add("valid")`. The fuzz target decodes hex and checks round-trip with `encoding/hex`. Print seed corpus entries using `fmt.Printf("Seed: %s\n", seed)`.
hints: f.Fuzz target takes *testing.T and fuzzed inputs

verification.failureMessage: Print seed corpus entries for the fuzz test.

steps.title: Test coverage analysis
steps.description: Write tests that achieve specific coverage targets. Use `go test -coverprofile=coverage.out` programmatically via `os/exec`. Call `go tool cover -html=coverage.out -o coverage.html`. Print coverage percentage using `fmt.Printf("Coverage: %.1f%%\n", pct)`.
hints: Use os/exec to run go test -coverprofile
Parse go test -cover output with strings.Contains
Run go tool cover to see detailed coverage

verification.failureMessage: Print coverage percentage from test results.

steps.title: TestMain for test orchestration
steps.description: Write a `TestMain(m *testing.M)` function that sets up a database (simulated map), runs tests with `m.Run()`, and tears down. Use `os.Exit` with the return value. Print setup and teardown messages using `fmt.Println`.
hints: TestMain runs in the main goroutine of the test binary
os.Exit(code) must be called with the result

steps.title: Table-driven tests with subtests
steps.description: Write a table-driven test using an anonymous slice of test cases, each with `name`, `input`, and `want`. Run each case with `t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) { ... })`. Print test names and pass/fail using `fmt.Printf("%s: %v\n", tc.name, passed)`.
hints: t.Run creates subtests with independent pass/fail
Print each subtest name and result

verification.failureMessage: Print each subtest name and whether it passed.
